title: Seal operator grants, KMS consent optimizer, and residency audit bridge
author: Mei Chen
release_notes: Adds timebound sealed operator grants, a KMS consent decision optimizer, and a residency delta audit bridge. No API breaking changes; rollout gated behind feature flags and a staged canary.
description: Background: We observed two recurring compliance burdens: (1) operator sessions and delegated operator credentials were overly permissive and lacked verifiable origin/POPs (proof-of-possession) which complicates audits and investigations; (2) frequent KMS consent calls from high-throughput paths increased cost and added latency for hot operator flows; additionally, customers requested compact residency audit exports that only include incremental deltas for efficient downstream ingestion. This PR implements three coordinated capabilities to address those gaps in a backwards-compatible way: 1) Sealed operator grants: an RBAC v2 policy extension and token envelope that attaches a signed, timebound assertion to operator grants (operator-claim + sealed metadata). The envelope is opaque to callers but verifiable by our operator-proxy and audit pipeline; it allows offline verification during incident postmortems and enforces short-lived, single-use grants for dangerous operations. 2) KMS consent optimizer: a bounded TTL decision cache and probabilistic refresher that reduces synchronous KMS consent validations on hot paths while preserving revalidation semantics for long-running flows. The cache is keyed by (operator, service, scope, residency-tag) and integrates with multi-provider KMS abstractions so fallbacks remain correct. 3) Residency audit bridge (delta exporter): a separate audit sink that emits residency-related audit deltas (region pin changes, sealed grant issuance, KMS consent samples) to a compact append-only export format (newline-delimited JSON with v1 header). The exporter supports batching, per-tenant opt-in, and integrity fingerprints for downstream verification. Design notes and rollout: - Backwards compatibility: Default behavior unchanged. Sealed grants are emitted only when the feature-flag "sealed-operator-grants" is enabled for a tenant; the audit bridge is opt-in per-tenant via tenancy config. The KMS consent optimizer is enabled globally with conservative TTLs and a feature to disable on a per-service level. - Security model: Sealed grants are signed by a short-lived service key (rotated via our KMS rotation process). Operator-proxy verifies signatures and enforces single-use semantics; replay protection is implemented via a bounded in-memory LRU with audit-backed fallback to the residency audit bridge. - Migration: Existing operator tokens remain valid until expiry. A migration job (scripts/migrations/emit-seal-claims) will seed sealed grants for active operator sessions during the canary window. - Testing and validation: Unit tests for RBAC rule translation, integration tests for operator-proxy verification, KMS integration tests with multi-provider simulation, and an end-to-end canary with perf-canary that measures added tail latencies. Checklist: [x] RBAC v2 schema change and translator mapping [x] operator-proxy middleware and verification [x] KMS consent cache with eviction policy and metrics [x] residency delta exporter + export contract docs [x] feature flags and canary rollout plan [x] migrations and one-off seed job [x] thorough unit/integration/e2e tests What changed (high-level): - New RBAC schema extension (sealed_grant metadata) and translator hook for policy compiler - operator-proxy: sealed grant verifier, replay guard, enforcement hooks - platform/kms: consent cache + metrics & instrumentation; fallbacks preserved - audit-writer: residency-delta exporter and compact export format (v1) - CLI: tenant opt-in flag and migration script - docs: design doc + example audit consumer schema See related tickets: ENG-2864 (sealed grants design), SEC-112 (compliance export contract), SUP-4512 (customer request for residency delta export).
